lesson.title: The Full Left-Walk
lesson.subtitle: je te vois, tu me comprends, il nous écoute — direct object pronouns walking before the verb.

hook.title: The Full Left-Walk: Direct Objects Across Every Person
hook.content: Direct object pronouns walk left of the verb across all persons: me/m' ('me'), te/t' ('you'), le/l' ('him/it'), la/l' ('her/it'), nous ('us'), vous ('you'), les ('them'). And in an infinitive chain (Je veux te voir, Je vais l'inviter), the pronoun stands right in front of the infinitive!

footnotes.title: Why 'I am waiting for you' is simply Je t'attends
footnotes.content: Because attendre already has 'for' built inside its meaning, 'you' is a direct object: te elides before attends → Je t'attends!

pattern.title: Single Verb: Pronoun Before Verb; Infinitive Chain: Pronoun Before Infinitive
pattern.content: Place direct object pronouns before the conjugated verb or before the infinitive.
pattern.linguist_note: Modern French places object clitics immediately before the lexical infinitive in modal/aspectual constructions.
pattern.trap_note: Don't add pour in 'I am waiting for you' (*J'attends pour toi) — use a direct left-walking pronoun: Je t'attends!

exercises.prompt: Match each French sentence with its English meaning:

matching_pairs.german: I am going to invite you

exercises.target_answer: I see you, I am waiting for you, Are you listening to me?, He understands us, I am going to invite you
exercises.meaning: Je te vois, Je t'attends (no 'for' needed!), Tu m'écoutes ? (no 'to' needed!), Il nous comprend, Je vais t'inviter (before infinitive!)
exercises.explanation: me, te, le, la elide to m', t', l' before a vowel; in infinitive chains, the pronoun hugs the infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Where does 'you' (te) go in 'I want to see you tonight'?
options: Je veux voir te ce soir
Je veux te voir ce soir
Je te veux voir ce soir
exercises.target_answer: Je veux te voir ce soir
exercises.meaning: I want to see you tonight
exercises.explanation: te is the object of voir, so it stands right in front of voir: Je veux te voir!

exercises.prompt: What is the word-for-word structure of 'Je vais l'inviter'?
exercises.natural: I am going to invite him/her
options: I am going to invite him/her
exercises.explanation: l' stands right in front of the infinitive inviter.

exercises.idea: I am waiting for you at the station
cues: at the station → à la gare
exercises.meaning: I am waiting for you at the station
exercises.explanation: te elides before attends: Je t'attends.

diagnosis.cue: attendre needs no 'for', and te elides to t': Je t'attends.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Est-ce que vous me comprenez bien
exercises.target_answer: Est-ce que vous me comprenez bien
exercises.affirmation: You placed me right before comprenez!

summary.outcome: Place direct object pronouns before conjugated verbs and before infinitives.

use_example.german: Je t'attends ici et je vais t'aider.
use_example.english: I'm waiting for you here and I'm going to help you.

summary.takeaway: Single verb: Je te vois; Infinitive chain: Je veux te voir.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([2302] lui & leur): see how The Full Left-Walk leads directly into lui & leur.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "I am waiting for you at the station" in French:
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Je t'attends à la gare" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of The Full Left-Walk.

me.etymology_derivation: Elides to m' before a vowel: il m'écoute.

te.etymology_derivation: Elides to t' before a vowel: je t'aime.

le.etymology_derivation: Latin ille 'that one' → il → le. English 'the' walked the same road — both are worn-down pointers.

la.etymology_derivation: ille's feminine illa → la. Before a vowel it loses its a: l'opinion.

nous.etymology_derivation: Latin nōs — English keeps the root in nostrum.

vous.etymology_derivation: Latin vōs 'you all' promoted to politeness — the same T–V ladder as German Sie and English's lost 'ye'.

voir.context_translation: I'm going to see my friend.
voir.etymology_derivation: Latin vidēre lost its middle d: vedere → veoir → voir.

comprendre.etymology_derivation: To understand is literally 'to grasp together'.

inviter.context_translation: Do you want to invite Marie?

attendre.context_translation: I am waiting for the train.
attendre.etymology_derivation: Latin attendere 'to stretch toward'. In French it means to wait for — with no preposition 'for' needed!
